title: What to buy
sub: All the electronics and hardware for the dash, besides the printed parts: the display head, the interface box, the small circuit parts, the screws and rubber, the phase 1 logger and the printing. Exact items are in COMPONENTS.md, the circuits in ELECTRONICS.md.

groups.label: Display head: electronics
groups.note: Buy the items marked "model fits this" exactly: the housing is modelled around them.

items.name: Waveshare ESP32-S3 2.8" round display, 480 x 480
items.for: The screen and the head's processor (ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-2.8C, or the no-touch ESP32-S3-LCD-2.8C)

items.name: u-blox NEO-M8N GPS module
items.for: GPS speed, trip and clock (its own 25 mm antenna isn't used)
items.note: Also Robocraze's NEO-M8N with active ceramic antenna (about ₹1,731). Avoid the "for Pixhawk" round pucks.

items.name: 18 x 18 mm active GPS patch antenna, IPEX (u.FL) lead
items.for: Lies flat at the top inside the housing, facing the sky

items.name: BH1750 light sensor (GY-302)
items.for: Automatic screen brightness

items.name: SN65HVD230 CAN transceiver modules, 3-pack
items.for: One in the head, two in the interface box (bike bus and dash bus)

items.name: WS2812B 5050 RGB LEDs on 10 mm round boards ("with heatsink")
items.for: The 8 tell-tales in the face

items.name: 74HCT125 quad buffer (DIP-14)
items.for: Turns the board's 3.3 V LED signal into 5 V

items.name: Translucent white UV resin (pen, or clear resin + white pigment)
items.for: Fills the icon cut-outs flush, diffuses the LEDs

items.name: GX12 4-pin aviation plug and panel socket + 1 m of 4-core shielded cable (0.5 mm²)
items.for: The cable from the head to the interface box

items.name: Espressif ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1-N8
items.for: The box's processor: two CAN controllers (bike bus, dash bus)
items.note: Robu, Hubtronics and Evelta usually list it for much less.

items.name: MPU-6050 motion sensor (GY-521)
items.for: Lean angle and g-force (fixed to the frame)

items.name: 12 V to 5 V 3 A sealed converter (Envistia)
items.for: Powers everything (8–24 V in)
items.note: Any sealed 8–36 V input 5 V 3 A converter of the same size works too.

items.name: 16-pin OBD-II female socket with shell (STAR055)
items.for: The OBD+ port (the bike's CAN bus, as in cars)

items.name: GX12 6-pin panel sockets + metal dust caps
items.for: The 3 expansion slots

items.name: DS18B20 waterproof temperature probe, 1 m
items.for: Air temperature, outside the box in the shade

items.name: The bike-side 18-pin cluster plug
items.for: The adapter harness, so no bike wires are cut
items.where: Its part number isn't known yet: phase 1 photos will identify it, or take one from a used cluster.

groups.label: Circuit parts (both boxes)
groups.note: For the circuits in ELECTRONICS.md, all through-hole for hand soldering.

items.name: PCF8574 I/O expander board (I2C)
items.for: Reads the 8 optocoupler inputs

items.name: PC817 optocouplers
items.for: The lamp and switch inputs (bike's 12 V kept away from the chip)

items.name: IRF4905 P-channel MOSFET (TO-220)
items.for: The power latch's switch

items.name: BC547 NPN transistors
items.for: The power latch

items.name: Diodes: 1N4148 (10), BAT85 (5), 1N4744A 15 V zener (1), SS34 Schottky (1)
items.for: Latch, input clamps, the head's power input

items.name: P6KE24A TVS diode
items.for: Clamps voltage spikes from the bike

items.name: Self-resetting fuses (PTC): 3 x 1 A, 3 x 0.5 A, 1 x 2 A, 1 x 1.5 A, 1 x 0.1 A
items.for: Expansion slots, OBD+ port, the head's cable, the gear sensor

items.name: Inline blade fuse holder + 3 A fuses
items.for: The main feed from the battery

items.name: Resistor kit (1/4 W) + 2 x 1 W resistors (100 Ω)
items.for: Dividers, pull-ups; the fuel sender's pull-up (final value after phase 1)

items.name: Capacitors: 100 nF ceramic (20), 470 µF 35 V, 1000 µF 10 V
items.for: Filtering

items.name: 3-pin jumpers, header pins, IC socket, JST-XH connectors
items.for: Plug-in modules and the input jumpers

items.name: Perfboard, about 9 x 15 cm and 5 x 7 cm
items.for: The interface box's board, the head's small board

items.name: Hook-up wire (24 AWG), 30 AWG wire-wrap wire, heat shrink
items.for: Wiring; chaining the LEDs

items.name: Conformal coating spray
items.for: Protects the boards from damp

items.name: M2 x 6 screws
items.for: Display to carrier

items.name: M3 heat-set inserts (5.7 mm long, 4.2 mm hole) + M3 x 10 pan-head screws
items.for: The back cover

items.name: M4 heat-set inserts (5.6 mm hole): 4 x 8 mm long, 4 x 6 mm long
items.for: The bar clamps and their feet

items.name: M4 x 14 bolts + rubber washers, M4 x 20 bolts
items.for: Feet to the cover (from inside), the clamps (up from below)

items.name: 2 mm rubber sheet (or print the pads in TPU)
items.for: The pads between the clamps' feet and the cover
items.local: Nagdevi Street or a rubber/seal shop

items.name: M4 heat-set inserts (8 mm) + M4 x 14 bolts
items.for: Cover to the cluster adapter

items.name: M6 bolts and nuts, about M6 x 16–20
items.for: The adapter to your cluster bracket (one per hole)

items.name: M5 x 20 bolt + nyloc nut, 2 x M4 x 20 bolts and nuts
items.for: The GoPro-style joint and its clamp

items.name: 1 mm rubber strip
items.for: Inside the bar clamps

items.name: 0.8 mm closed-cell foam sheet (or print the gasket in TPU)
items.for: The foam ring under the face, on the glass's border

items.name: Double-sided foam tape
items.for: The GPS module and CAN board on the carrier

groups.label: Phase 1: the CAN logger
groups.note: The ESP32-C6, a CAN transceiver and the GPS above are reused here first.

items.name: Royal Enfield 6-pin to 16-pin OBD-II adapter
items.for: Reaches the bike's service socket. Check your socket's colour first, and ask the seller to confirm it fits the Meteor 350

buy.note: ("16 PIN to 6 PIN for Himalayan and Hunter")

items.name: 16-pin OBD-II male plug to open wires (pigtail)
items.for: So nothing is cut on the bike

items.name: microSD module (SPI, 3.3 V) + an 8–32 GB microSD card
items.for: The logs

items.name: 12 V to USB car charger + USB-C cable
items.for: Powers the logger from the OBD socket

items.name: Printing: the shell, carrier, cover, trim ring and the mount
items.for: PETG for a prototype, ASA for the final parts. Upload the STLs for an exact quote

totals: about ₹5,600–8,100 using Indian electronics stores for the ESP32-C6, ₹7,300–9,800 on Amazon.in / Flipkart only
about ₹14,000–17,000 using Indian electronics stores for the display and the ESP32-C6, ₹21,000–24,000 on Amazon.in / Flipkart only
note: Listed prices from 2026-11-23; (est.) = not checked on a listing. Tools you'll want: a multimeter, a 12 V 3 A bench supply, a soldering iron; optionally a USB logic analyser (₹500–800 (est.)).
